messages:
mike: quick one — noticed a recurring fallback issue: when a request served by Hosted falls back to Dedicated/Private, the target env frequently rejects the auth token (aud mismatch / tenant scoped). we should decide a clean contract for credential semantics during cross-mode fallbacks.

anna: +1. saw this in the payments flow yesterday. hosted token had aud:api.hosted and private runtime expected aud:private-runtime. request failed and we retried, adding ~250ms. :grimacing: 

mike: two user-facing constraints: 1) we cannot leak long-lived hosted admin creds into customer private envs, 2) fallbacks must be fast (<~100ms ideally).

renato: proposal: a small translation layer in the control plane that mints ephemeral bridge tokens scoped to the target runtime on fallback. TTL short (30s), aud set to target, and limited scopes (only inference call). no secret material leaves the control plane; it only issues a scoped jwt signed by our bridge key. sketch: 
```yaml
# fallback exchange (sketch)
POST /v1/fallback-token
body: { original_token, target: "private:tenant-123" }
resp: { bridge_token: "jwt", ttl: 30 }

# downstream call uses: Authorization: Bearer bridge_token
```

claire: major caveat: private deployments may have their own KMS/tenant keys and strict audit requirements. we must emit full audit events and avoid any flow that would let us decrypt customer data. this bridge token should never grant data-decryption rights, only inference request invocation.

tara: also consider proof-of-possession (PoP) or mTLS between runtime and control plane for the exchange so private runtimes can verify the token was requested by an authorized control plane node. aud/iss mapping + cert thumbs might be enough.

anna: performance idea: cache bridge tokens per tenant-target for a tiny window (e.g., 5s) to reduce chattiness. cache invalidation keyed by route config. must log cache hits for billing/telemetry.

renato: agreed. implementation plan: add a middleware in routing layer to detect fallback, call bridge-token service (or cache), attach token header and forward. provide opt-out via routing policy (some enterprises won't allow any token translation).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary started for credential-translator v0.1 to eng-infra-qa (3 instances) — 1764912398

mike: we should add a strict opt-in flag in tenant manifest: "allow_bridge_token": "false|true" and default to false for Private. update docs + console flag.

renato: RFC checklist I'm thinking: goals, threat model (what we will never do), token shape, TTL defaults, audit events, opt-out, perf budget. I'll draft and ping @mike and @claire for review.

claire: add a section on KMS constraints and what we will log. also include guidance for customers running air-gapped stacks.

tara: curious about PoP overhead — if we can't get mTLS everywhere, maybe signed nonce exchange with short TTL is a lighter fallback. worth a perf microbenchmark.

mike: action items: renato write RFC, run perf microbenchmarks for token exchange + cached path (<10ms target), claire write audit/KMS doc fragment, anna validate failure-mode test in payments flow.

anna: will add a simple test case to the payments integration suite and run against canary.

renato: thanks — pinging when draft is ready. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: note: incident-bot rule removed for this thread — fallback auth noise threshold lowered.
